documents: Baxter, White, Brenna & Ohneiser (2022), Pre-eruption magma staging at the long-lived intraplate Dunedin Volcano, New Zealand, Terra Nova 34:253-263 (published PDF)

entry.evidence: It remains unclear how these larger, more-complex volcanoes are born within regions of dispersed volcanism.

sequences.source_document: Baxter et al. 2022, Terra Nova 34:253-263 (published PDF)

steps.action: States two conflicting published generalizations of volcano lifecycles as rivals: primitive magmas erupt first, or evolved magmas erupt first.
steps.quote: Current understanding of a volcano's lifecycle are encapsulated in two, conflicting, generalizations

steps.action: Poses the question of how large, complex volcanoes are born within fields of dispersed small volcanoes.
steps.quote: It remains unclear how these larger, more-complex volcanoes are born within regions of dispersed volcanism.

steps.action: Selects Otapahi, where the oldest-dated Dunedin Volcano rocks (a dike dated 16.0 Ma by others) cut shallow submarine pyroclastic deposits, as the site of study.
steps.quote: The oldest-known rocks of the DV are exposed at Otapahi

steps.action: Maps field relations, notes the absence of igneous lithics in older diatremes and the extensive mingling of diverse dikes, and samples for petrography, whole-rock geochemistry, EPMA and magnetic polarity.
steps.quote: Compositionally and texturally diverse dikes are extensively mingled together, forming dike complexes

steps.action: Compares Otapahi immobile-element ratios with compiled Dunedin Volcano data and finds they exceed most of the volcano-wide range.
steps.quote: The range of immobile element ratios for dikes from Otapahi exceed the vast majority of Zr/Ti ratios reported for volcanic rocks from DV

steps.action: Checks the alteration-affected major-element (TAS) classification against modal mineralogy and immobile trace-element ratios, which reveal a basanite and probable phonolites.
steps.quote: Modal abundances indicate the presence of a basanite dike at Otapahi, not represented by whole-rock major elements

steps.action: Measures plagioclase element profiles by EPMA and finds disequilibrium textures and zoning of varying complexity, especially in mafic dikes.
steps.quote: Crystals from most of the mafic and intermediate dikes display disequilibrium textures and zoning.

steps.action: Tests the magnetic polarity of the pumice subunits and three dikes; all are normal, which places them within C5Cn1 or C5Cn2, consistent with the Ar-Ar age.
steps.quote: All are of normal polarity, narrowing the date, within 40Ar/39Ar date error range

steps.action: Argues from the absence of older igneous lithics and from peperite and magma-mingling textures that these are the earliest products and that diverse magmas were emplaced at the same time.
steps.quote: earlier dikes must have still been partially molten for mingling to occur

steps.action: Takes published dike-cooling observations and models to bound the time within which mingling could occur.
steps.quote: Dikes have been observed to cool below 500°C 20 years after intrusion

steps.action: Excludes derivation of the diverse magmas from a single static magma body evolving over centuries to millennia.
steps.quote: This thermally limited timeframe precludes derivation of the different magmas from a single static magma body

steps.action: Concludes from immobile ratios and REE that Otapahi's compositional diversity equals that of the whole Dunedin Volcano sequence.
steps.quote: demonstrate Otapahi's compositional diversity is equal to the diversity recorded from entire DV's sequence

steps.action: Infers magma mixing from pumice zoning, simple mixing models for intermediate dikes, disequilibrium textures and complex crystal profiles.
steps.quote: Magma mixing processes are inferred for Otapahi from chemical zoning of pumice deposit

steps.action: Lists rival origins for the alkali- and trace-element-enriched samples without discriminating among them.
steps.quote: smaller degrees of partial melting, wall-rock interactions, longer residence/evolution times, or some combination

steps.action: Infers a qualitative plumbing model: mafic accumulation at the Moho, a leaky middle crust, and magma stalled at structural traps in the shallow crust, each batch evolving separately (Figure 3).
steps.quote: We infer accumulation of mafic magmas at the MOHO

steps.action: Compares the qualitative plumbing model with published quantitative storage depths elsewhere in the volcano and reports agreement.
steps.quote: Their quantitative modelling of the broader volcano's plumbing system concurs with our qualitative inferences

steps.action: Proposes that multiple failed eruptions build a subterranean magmatic system before surface activity, an analogue at smaller scale of continental arcs.
steps.quote: we suggest their compositional diversity may first develop due to multiple failed eruptions

steps.action: Compares the early Otapahi compositions with the range erupted over the volcano's later history and finds they cover it.
steps.quote: These compositions cover the range erupted over the remainder of the volcano's activity

steps.action: Infers that the phonolitic pumice eruption destabilized the maturing system and mobilized deeper magmas, perhaps through a downward-propagating decompression wave.
steps.quote: Eruption of phonolite magma to form the PLb disrupted and destabilized a maturing magmatic system

steps.action: Rejects, for the Dunedin Volcano, both the primitive-first and the evolved-first lifecycle models.
steps.quote: are not appropriate for the DV

steps.action: Refines the model to tiered reservoirs that failed to integrate over 5 Myr and never formed a transcrustal system.
steps.quote: suggest a system of tiered reservoirs (Maclennan, 2019) failing to fully integrate through millions of years

steps.action: Keeps the claim that a complex, weakly interconnected magma system developed very early and persisted for 5 Myr.
steps.quote: a complex weakly interconnected magma system developed very early

No; the plumbing system is inferred from rock traces

Primitive-first versus evolved-first lifecycle; a single static magma body

tree.question: 6b
tree.answer: The same range of magmas erupted repeatedly over 5 Myr (compiled data)
Partly: alteration checked with immobile elements and modal mineralogy; polarity consistent with the Ar-Ar age
Both lifecycle models rejected for the Dunedin Volcano; early mature tiered system kept as best explanation

end.claim: A complex, weakly interconnected magma system of multiple deep and shallow reservoirs existed as the Dunedin Volcano began erupting, and it set the pattern for 5 Myr of activity.

decisive_move.sentence: The mingling and peperite evidence that compositionally diverse magmas were emplaced contemporaneously, among the earliest products, turns compositional diversity into evidence for a pre-existing mature plumbing system.

gates.evidence: The rival lifecycle models are stated up front, and the choice of the oldest outcrop targets them, but sampling was general fieldwork with no stated prediction (p. 253-254). The diversity result could have failed, for example if only primitive or only evolved early products had been found, but the mechanism (failed eruptions, tiered reservoirs) is qualitative and is not tested (p. 257-261). Nothing is reported as fixed before the data.

Aerial image with superimposed photogrammetry of the outcrop
Pyrolite Python package for geochemical plots

novelty_claims.quote: provide new information about how long-lived, low-output composite volcanoes originate and develop through their lives
display one of these dikes as the most extensively fractionated from the DV, exceeding the range reported from other known DV phonolites

limits: The supplementary files S1-S3 (methods, figures, results) were not supplied, so the analytical procedures, the mixing models and the polarity data cannot be checked here. No review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded. The claim that these are the earliest products rests partly on a companion paper listed as submitted (Baxter & White). The plumbing model is qualitative and is supported by agreement with published quantitative modelling elsewhere in the volcano, not by modelling of Otapahi samples. Sub-claims: contemporaneous emplacement of diverse magmas is best_explanation (from textures and cooling timescales); the failed-eruption origin of the system is a suggestion with status none (inference); unintegrated tiered reservoirs over 5 Myr is best_explanation, resting on cited compilations; the rival origins of the enriched samples are left open (no_conclusion on that sub-question). No uncertainties are given for the geochemical data in the main text. There are minor citation inconsistencies: Price 1973 in the caption and Price 1975 in the legend, and Coombs et al. (1986) in the text against Coombs & Reay 1986 in the references. Whether any analyses were planned before the fieldwork cannot be determined (inference).

disagreements.target: Primitive-first lifecycle model (Khalaf et al., 2018; Sato et al., 1990)
disagreements.support: The earliest, contemporaneously emplaced Otapahi rocks already span primitive to highly evolved compositions.
disagreements.quote: Models in which a volcano commences activity by erupting primitive material (Khalaf et al., 2018; Sato et al., 1990)

disagreements.target: Evolved-first lifecycle model (Pánisová et al., 2018; Panter et al., 1997)
disagreements.support: Primitive and evolved magmas were emplaced together at the onset, so evolved lavas did not come first alone.
disagreements.quote: or with emplacement of evolved lavas (Pánisová et al., 2018; Panter et al., 1997), are not appropriate for the DV

disagreements.target: Central volcanoes of continental arcs (Annen et al., 2006)
disagreements.support: Subterranean system-building is similar, but here very diverse magmas erupted nearly synchronously among the earliest rocks.
disagreements.quote: Unlike central volcanoes of continental arcs, here there was a great diversity of compositions

disagreements.target: Transcrustal magma system concept (Cashman et al., 2017)
disagreements.support: Repeated eruption of the same magma range over 5 Myr implies reservoirs that never became vertically connected.
disagreements.quote: never developing the vertical connectivity of a transcrustal magma system (Cashman et al., 2017)

alternatives_considered.chosen: Immobile trace-element ratios (Zr/Ti, REE) and modal mineralogy for classification

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Smaller degrees of partial melting; wall-rock interaction; longer residence/evolution times
Primitive-first lifecycle; evolved-first lifecycle; single static magma body
alternatives_considered.reason: Contemporaneous emplacement of diverse magmas and dike-cooling timescales
